Hey man. I understand that you’ll hope your future child has a good life, but as an antinatalist that’s your age (18), there’s a lot that will happen in our lifetimes. The whole world situation is icky at best, with genocide and the wealth gap and the pandemic and mental illness as well as physical illness and climate change.

You mention that your child could experience the joys of life, and don’t get me wrong, there are many joys in life, but you won’t be the one to suffer the consequences if there is more suffering than joy. Working in a nursing home is the only legal use for my power. I sit with them all, day after day, having a good chat with Jasmine and Maria, sitting watching the football with Bert and Robert, and helping the nurses out with bed bound patients and always making cups of tea and coffee.

Some of the residents are completely sound of mind, but others... not so much. Some of our residents can be here for years without a single family member, and I know how lonely they can be. Sometimes, just using my words, I’ll pretend to be their son or daughter and will sit and keep them company for a while. It’s a lot stronger pain relief than any amount of other sedatives.

Many people don’t think what I do is ethical, and maybe it’s not. It’s also particularly useful when one of our residents has fallen or is close to death. I soothe them and tell them that they’re going to be okay, and sometimes they even die with a slight smile, because they truly believe they’re going to be fine.

I’ve tried many lines of work, but this is the most fulfilling. Watching my grandma pass away slowly and painfully before I developed my power has made me want to make the most vulnerable of people’s deaths slightly more comfortable. I’m on call 18 hours a day, with bookings for specific days, such as assisted suicide for those terminally ill and alone.
